title: One smooth hypersurface slice at a separable closed fibre point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $x\in X$ map to $s\in S$, with $x$ closed in the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume that $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite (finite-dimensional as a vector space) and separable algebraic [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and that $\dim_x(X_s)=d$ for an integer $d\geq1$, with dimension at a point as in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then there exist an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and an effective Cartier divisor $D\hookrightarrow U$ [def-trf-effective-cartier-center, def-weil-closed-immersion] containing $x$, such that the composite $D\to U\to X\to S$ is smooth and $\dim_x(D_s)=d-1$. Here $x$ in $D$ denotes the unique point mapping to the specified $x\in U$.

source.place: Tag 057F, lemma-slice-smooth-once-separable-residue-field-extension, specialized to a closed fibre point of positive dimension; Tag 057C, lemma-slice-smooth-given-element, proof, displayed dimension drop for the chosen hypersurface.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(s)$ and $L=\kappa(x)$. Apply [lem-trf-separable-smooth-cotangent-germ] with the given $d\geq1$ and finite separable $L/k$. Obtain its affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ over $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the smooth finite-type fibre algebra $C=k\otimes_B A$, the regular Noetherian local ring $R=C_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ with residue field $L$, and $h\in\mathfrak m_x$ with nonzero relative differential. Its fibre image $\bar h$ belongs to the maximal ideal of $R$ and is a nonzerodivisor.

Apply [lem-trf-prescribed-germ-smooth-cartier-cut] to this specified $h$, with prescribed neighbourhood $W$. Its two hypotheses on the germ are exactly the conclusions of step 1. Obtain an affine $U\subseteq W$ and $a\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ with germ $h$, whose principal closed subscheme $D$ contains $x$, is effective Cartier in $U$, and is smooth over $S$. The same lemma identifies $\mathcal O_{D_s,x}$ with $R/(\bar h)$, with residue field $L$. Thus the local equation and the point are preserved by the shrinking.

source.place: Tag 057C, lemma-slice-smooth-given-element, affine realization of a prescribed germ.

proof.text: Since $R$ is Noetherian local and $\bar h$ is a nonzerodivisor in its maximal ideal, [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] gives $\dim(R/(\bar h))+1=\dim R$. Apply [lem-kun-dimension-formula] on the finite-type $k$-scheme $W_s=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and on the following finite-type chart of $D_s$. Choose $x\in D_W(t)\subseteq U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], and identify this open with $\operatorname{Spec}A_t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]. Let $b\in A_t$ restrict $a$. Restricting its principal ideal gives the open $D'=D\cap D_W(t)=\operatorname{Spec}(A_t/(b))$ of $D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the fibre ring of $D'$ is $k\otimes_B(A_t/(b))\cong C_{\bar t}/(b_s)$. Explicitly $\lambda\otimes[c/t^n]\mapsto[(\lambda\otimes c)/\bar t^n]$; the inverse sends $[(\lambda\otimes c)/\bar t^n]$ to $\lambda\otimes[c/t^n]$ and extends additively. The tensor, localization and quotient relations are respected: $\bar t$ is invertible and $b_s$ maps to zero. If $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ generate $C$ over $k$, their images together with $\bar t^{-1}$ generate this quotient, proving finite type. Its local ring at $x$ is $R/(\bar h)$ by step 2, and both charts have residue field $L$. Since $L/k$ is algebraic, its transcendence degree is zero: an algebraically independent nonempty set would contain a transcendental element. The dimension formula identifies their dimensions at $x$ with $\dim R$ and $\dim(R/(\bar h))$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] they are open fibre charts, and [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] identifies their dimensions at $x$ with $d$ and $\dim_xD_s$. Thus $\dim_xD_s+1=d$, giving $d-1$ since $d\geq1$. The point over $x$ is unique because a closed immersion is injective [def-weil-closed-immersion].

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_smooth_effectiveCartier_hypersurface_slice {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed {f.asFiber x}) (hfinite : @FiniteDimensional (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) _ _ (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra.toModule) (hseparable : @Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) _ _ (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hdim : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) : ∃ (U D : Scheme.{u}) (j : U ⟶ X) (i : D ⟶ U) (u : U) (xD : D), IsAffine U ∧ IsOpenImmersion j ∧ j u = x ∧ IsEffectiveCartierCenter i ∧ i xD = u ∧ Smooth (i ≫ j ≫ f) ∧ topologicalKrullDimAt ((i ≫ j ≫ f).asFiber xD) = ((d - 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
